SHERWELL, ARNOLD GUY.—B. 1891; ed. St. Edward's Schl. and Brasenose Coll., Oxford; M.A. (schl. of jurisprudence, hons. cls. III); called to bar (Inner Temple), 1914; asst. res., Nyasaland, 1914; mily. serv. in Africa, ment. in desps., 1915; practised at bar, 1920-25; dist. judge, Sudan, 1925; asst. advoc. gen. and legal advr. to Sudan govt., rlys. and steamers, 1928; govt. advoc., Palestine, Apr., 1929; relieving pres. of dist. cts., 1930; pres., dist. ct., 1935.

SHIELD, CHARLES GEOFFREY.—B. 1896; on mily. service (France) 1914-18; on staff, 1918-19; priv. secy. to gov., and clk. to couns., Seychelles, 1920.

SHIELDS, DR. T. DRUMMOND, M.C., M.P.—B. 1881; ed. Edinburgh Univ. (M.B., Ch. B.); served European War as offr. R. Scots.; in command, with rank as capt., one of trench mortar batteries of 9th (Scottish) Divn. (severely wounded); was a mem., Edinburgh town coun.; M.P., East Edinburgh since 1924; mem., sp. comm., Ceylon constitution, 1927; partly, under-sec., India Office, June, 1924; partly, under-sec. for cols., 1929-31.

SHILL, A. T.—B. 1898; on active serv. with Rifle Brig. and Dorset Regt., 1915-17; wounded; Imp. cust. and excise dept., 1919; also dep. supt., mercantile marine, recr. of wreck, regist., shipping, Lascar transfer offr., etc. asst. recr. gen., Gambia, Aug., 1928; ag. asst. col. sec., Apr. to Oct., 1929 and from July, 1931; contr., food and fuel, May, 1931; supervisor, cust. and excise dept., Mauritius, Apr., 1932.

SHIPWAY, WALTER ROBERT, M.B.E. (1924).—B. 1879; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd div. clk., and assigned to C.O., Dec., 1898; minor staff clk., 1911; registr. of col. laws, 1st Apr., 1922; staff offr., promotions, 19th Nov., 1928.

SHIRLEY, EVELYN PHILIP SEWALLS, O.B.E.—B. 1900; ed. St. Columbus Coll., Rathfarnham, Dublin and R. Mily. Coll., Camberley; joined R. Irish Fusiliers, Dec., 1918; N. Persia and Iraq, 1920; seconded, K.A.R., Jan., 1923; 2/1st K.A.R., Tanganyika and Somaliland Camel Corps; 3rd grade commr., Somaliland, Sept., 1929.

SHREWSBURY, HERBERT SUTCLIFFE, F.I.C., F.C.S.—B. 1878; ed. Newchurch Grammar Schl., Nottingham Univ.; asst. govt. analyst, Trini-
dad, 1910; prin. asst. govt. analyst, 1912; govt. analyst, 1920; author of various papers on orig. and analytical processes, and on agrl. and forensic chemistry.

SHUCKBURGH, Sir John Evelyn, K.C.M.G. (1922), C.B. (1818).—B. 1877; ed. Eton and King's Coll., Cambridge; B.A., 1899; M.A., 1906; apptd. jnr. clk., store dept., I.O., Oct., 1900; transf. to judi. and pub. dept., Mar., 1901; joint editor, "India Office List," Oct., 1901; priv. sec. to permant. under-sec. of state, July, 1902; senr. clk., polit. dept., Mar., 1903; asst. sec., polit. dept., Oct., 1912; sec., polit. dept., Mar., 1917; ag. asst. under sec. of state, C.O., 1st Mar., 1921; asst. under sec. of state, 1st Apr., 1924; dep. under sec. of state, 15th Aug., 1931.

SHUTE, Geoffrey Gay, B.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1892; ed. St. Andrew's Sch., Eastbourne, Uppingham and Clare Coll., Cambridge; asst. dist. offr., Nigeria, 1915; cl. I, admst. serv., 1930; prin. asst. sec., S. Prova., 1931; sec., S. Prova., 1933; staff grade, 1936.

SIDEBOTHAM, John Buddleth, B.A. (1914), M.A. (1920).—B. 1891; ed. King's Sch., Canterbury, and Gonville and Caius Coll., Cambridge (Stanhope exhibr., open class exhibr., 1911, school, 1912); 1st cls., theolog. tripso, pt. I., 1914; 2nd lieut., Home Counties R.E. (T.F.), 1914; lieut., 13th June, 1916; serv. in France, 1914-15; wounded, Apr., 1915; demob., 1919; ent. inland rev., Somerset House, 7th Feb., 1920; transf. to C.O. as asst. prin. under reconstruction scheme, Dec., 1922; sec., managing comttee, bureau of hygiene and trop. diseases, 1925; sec., East African guaranteed loan advisory comttee, 1927; pvt. sec. to partly. under-sec. of state for dom. affrs., 16th Sept., 1928; pvt. sec., perm. under sec. for the cols., 8th July, 1929, prin., 24th Jan., 1930; accomp. perm. under S. of S. for the Cols. (Sir J. Maffey) to W. Indies, 1936.

SIDLEY, William Henry Francis, B.A. (Trinity Coll., Dublin).—Cadet, R.I.C., Aug., 1903; 3rd cls. dist. inspr., Oct., 1908; 2nd cls., Feb., 1910; 1st cls., Aug., 1919; county inspr., Nov., 1920; served in R.I.C. until disbandment of that force, July, 1922; depot inspr. (1st cls.), Jamaica constab., Dec., 1922; ag. dep. inspr.-gen., Aug., 1923; dep. inspr.-gen., Deco., 1923; ag. inspr.-gen., June to Oct., 1925.

SILVESTER, J. M.—Asst. dist. commr., E.A.P., Dec., 1913; ag. dist. commr., Kenya, 1926.

SIMBY, Percy Arnold Tyndall.—B. 1892; ed. Sherborne and Queens' Coll., Cambridge; probationer, native dept., N. Rhodesia, July, 1914; asst. nat. commr., 1916; nat. commr., 1922; asst. mag., 1926; distr. offr., gr. I., 1935; ag. prov. commr., 1936.

SIMMONS, Benjamin Robert—Clk. in conservator of forest's office, E. conservancy, Transvaal, 1898; ag. dist. forest offr., Stutterheim, 1902; dist. forest offr., Stutterheim, 1906; ditto, George, 1914; 2nd grade conservator of forests, Transkeian conservancy, 1929; prin. forest offr. (forestry inspr.), Natal and Transkei, 1932; Western inspectorate, 1935.

SIMMONS, George Stanley, M.I.Mech.E., Chartered Mech. Engnr.—B. 1892; ed. Battersea Polytechnic; asst. loco. supt., Lancashire and Yorkshire's loco. supt., Togoland Milly. rly., Apr., 1917; asst. loco. supt., Gold Coast rly., May, 1920; dist. loco. supt., do., July, 1925; asst. ch. mech. engnr., do., Dec., 1926; ch. mech. engnr., do., Apr., 1934.

SIMMONS, Hon. Wm. Chas.—B. 1865; ed. at Collingwood Owen Sound High Schla.; B.A., Tor., called to the bar, N.W.T., 1900; elec. to legis. assm. of Alberta's bridge dist., 1905; resign., 1908; pres. sup. ct., Alberta, 12th Oct., 1910.

SIMMS, Henry, O.B.E. (1933), M.T., A.M.I.C.E. (1913).—B. 1881; nav. engr., Coast, 1908; navy, engr., Suez Lec., D.P.W., Cyprus, 1919; D.P.W., James Simpson, John—Imp. tel. ser., Ju., 1920; transf., post office, Cape of Good Hope, 1886; survr., posts and tele., May, 1929; survr. inspr., Aug., 1922; ch. pob. ser., July, 1934.

SIMS, George, M.A. (Oxon.), Edan.—B. 1908; ed. Chesterfield Grammar non-collegiate soc., Oxford; asst. nat. dept., Hong Kong, 1930; lect., tech. inst., 35; govt. exam., colloquial Cantonese headmast., govt. secondary sch., Cypr., sub-inspr., Basutoland Mounted Police, inspr., 1913; asst. commr., 1918; commr. and govt. sec., 1934.

SINCLAIR, Hon. John Ewen—K.C., local common schlr., mem. of swine coms., visited Europe in 1909; unacq. cand. P.E.I., 1908; el. to H.C., g.e., 1917; res. min. without portfolio in King admin., Dec., 1921; senator, June, 1930.

SINCLAIR, Hon. Sir J. R., Kt. Bach—B., 1851; ed. Dunedin High School barrister; M.L.C., N.Z., 1907 and rep. N.Z. on Dominion Royal Comm.

SINCLAIR-BURGESS, Major

WILLIAM LIVINGSTONE HATCHWELL (1935), Kt. Bach. (1934), C.B., C.M.G., D.S.O. (1916)—Lieut., N.Z. Staff Gr., 1911; adjt., 16th Waikato Regt., staff group, Mar., 1911; capt., June, 1911; as exchange offr. with Australian forces, 1913; brig.-major, 6th mil. div., left Australia with A.I.F., O.C., 1914; major (A.I.F.), 1914; commr. Australian F.A., Bde., with rank lieu.-col., 1916; commr. 4th Australian Div., rank brig.-gen., Aug., 1917; m. corp., corps, 1919; lieut.-col., Aug., 1920; offr., cent. commd., Nov., 1919; G.H.Q., Apr., 1922; dir., mil. intell., Jan., 1924; ch. of gen. st., with temp. rank col. on staff; ag. mil. forces, Sep., 1925; ch. of mil. forces, Apr., 1931; Croix d'officier Honour; awarded American Distinguished Service Medal, in despo.

SISNETT, Sir Herbert Donnell, Kt. Bach. (1927)—Coll., Barbados; called to the bar, May, 1896; practised at bar, 1897 to Feb., 1898; ag. j. Bridgetown, Barbados, Sept., 1898; ag. res. mag. for St. Anna, J., ag. priv. sec. to Sir A. Hemans, 1902, and priv. sec. to Mr. Oliphant, June to Nov., 1902; clk., Jamaica, Apl., 1903; ag. re. and Trelawny, Sept., 1903, Mar., 1904, do., Manchester, do., St. James and Trelawny, 1906; regiar-gen., Br. Hon. of Belize, Apl., 1907; ag. ad. just., Br. Hon., on several Br. Hon., 1907; stip. mag., 1913 held inquiry into Rose and was highly commended.
DOMINIONS OFFICE AND COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

1919-20; seconded, puisne judge, Jamaica, O; 1st puisne judge, 1921; ch. just., Br. nd., 1922; compiled Br. Hond. sup. ct. rules, 6; apptd. arbitrator by govts. of U.S.A. and Guatemala in case of P.W. Shufeldt v. the govt.

CITTAMPALAM, CATHIRAVELU, B.A. (Cantab.), Barrister-at-law (Middle Temple).—1898; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Feb., 1923; d., Kalutara kach., Mar., 1923; ditto, Kandy kach., Mar., 1925; office asst., Puttalam kach., 1926; pol. mag., Matara, Apr., 1928; ditto, Kottalam, Oct., 1929; asst. govt. agt., Kurunegala, Nov., 1929; dist. judge, Kegalle, July, 1931; asst. govt. agt., Kurunegala, July, 1932; do., Kottalam, May, 1934.

SKAN, D. A., M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., D.T.M., T.H. (Liv.).—B.1899; war serv., R.N.V.R., 1918; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1926.

SKEETE, CECIL CARRINGTON, B.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1900; ed. Harrison Coll., Barbados and sua Coll., Cambridge; 3rd class hon. nat. sci. pos pt. I., 1922; dipl. course, Sch. of Agr., Cambridge, 1922-23; asst. dir., agr., Barbados, pt., 1923; ag. dir., agr., in 1924 and 1925; st. dir., sci. and agr., Sept., 1925; ag. dir. i. and agr. on various occasions, 1926-29.

SKELETON, OSCAR DOUGLAS, M.A., Ph.D.—B. 78; ed. Orangeville and Cornwall High Schls., Queen's Univ. and Univ. of Chicago; counsellor, pt. of external affrs., 13th July, 1924; under-c. of state for external affrs., 30th Mar., 1925.

SKENE, CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1889; ed. St. Paul's Schl. and Wren's; asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, Nov., 1912; seconded for serv. in col. sec.'s Ace., 1912-13; dist. comsnr., G. Coast, Nov., 112; col. sec.'s office, 1912-15; priv. sec. to ag. pv., 1914; ag. dist. comsnr., Ashanti, 1916-18; st. comsnr., Oct., 1918; ag. pol. mag., Dec., 1922; dep. prov. comsnr., July, 1927; prov. comsnr., Sept., 1928; ag. sec., native affrs. Apr., 1930 and Apr. to Oct., 1932; ag. dep. col. so., June-Sept., 1930.

SKINNER, ARTHUR DONALD WILLIAM.—B. 390; ed. Bedford Schl.; 4th clk., col. sec.'s office, Antigua, Aug., 1914; sub-inspr. of schools, St. Kitts-Nevis, Apl., 1915; o/o cadet corps, St. Kitts-Nevis, 1917; ag. inspr. of schls., Leeward Is., Apr., 1918 to Feb., 1920; clk. o/o comsnr., clk. of couns. and educnl. dist. offr., Montserrat, Feb.-Oct., 1920; 1st clk., col. sec.'s office, clk. of couns., Antigua and suplt., govt. printing office, Leeward Is., Nov., 1920; ag. asst. ol. sec. and ag. clk. of couns. Leeward Is. on various occasions 1921-24; bursar, Achimota Coll., Gold Coast, 1927; ag. prin., Prince of Wales Coll., July to Sept., 1929; asst. col. sec., Sept., 1931; g. clk. couns., May to June, 1932.

SKINNER, HUGH WELBY.—B. 1894; war serv., 1914-19; served in France, India, Mesopotamia; apt., T.A. res., gen. list, R.A.; appt. col. audit lept., 1923; asst. audr., Nyasaland, 1923; asst. audr., Nigeria, 1926; col. audit, 1930; asst. audr., Gold Coast, 1935.

SKINNER, LESLIE ERNEST.—B.1890; Gloucestershire R.F.A., 1908 to 1910; B.S.A. Pol., 1910 to 1913; E.A.P. pol., Sept., 1913; asst. supt., 1915; staff offr. to inspr. gen. of pol. and prisons, Kenya Colony and Uganda Prot., 1920 to 1922; supt., pol., Nyasaland, 1922; ag. ch. comsnr. pol. and ch. inspr., prisons, 1923 to 1924; asst. commdt., pol., Zanzibar, 1924; ag. comsnr., pol. and gov. prisons on various occasions, 1925-35.

SKINNER, ROBERT BURNELL, M.B.E. (1933).—B.1893; ed. Bedford Modern Schl.; held various minor appts., Leeward Is., 1910-20; ch. elk. to admr., and clk., couns., St. Kitts-Nevis, Nov., 1920; ch. clk. to admr. and elk., couns., Dominica, Nov., 1924; sec., loan bd., May, 1926; mem., Roseau town bd., Apr., 1927; comsnt., income tax, May, 1927; ptye. sec. to Sir Eustace Fiennes, Nov., 1927 to June, 1929; ag. treas., Dominica, June to Sept., 1929; offl. mem., exec. and leg. couns., Dominica, June to Sept., 1929; O.A.G., Montserrat, Feb., 1930; ag. treas. and offl. mem., exec. and leg. couns., May to Sept., 1930; treas., Antigua and fedl. treas., Mar., 1931; offl. mem., fedl. exec. coun. and gen. leg. coun.; mem., exec. and leg. coun., Antigua; dep. treas. and comsnr., income tax, Trinidad, Mar., 1934; ag. treas., Aug.-Dec., 1936.

SLATER, SIR ALEXANDER RANSFORD, G.C.M.G. (1933), K.C.M.G. (1924); C.M.G. (1916); C.B.E. (1918).—B. 1874; ed. at King Ed. schl., Birmingham, and Emm. Coll., Camb. (scholar); B.A. 1897 (30th wrangler); cadet, Ceylon, Nov., 1898; extra offr. asst. govt. agt., W. P., Aug., 1899; 2nd asst., P.M.G., Mar., 1900; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Dec., 1901; on spec. duty at camp for prisoners of war Diyatalawa, July, 1902; ag. 2nd asst. col. sec., Jan., 1903; clk. legis. coun., May, 1904; dist. judge, Badulla, Apl., 1906; additional asst. col. sec. and elk., legis. couns., Apl., 1907; on special deptn. to Straits and F.M.S., Jan., 1908; 2nd asst. col. sec., Feb., 1908; ag. prin. asst. col. sec., Dec., 1909; dep. collr. of cust., Colombo, Sept., 1910; joint comsnr. to report on salaries of pub. serv., Nov., 1911; prin. asst. col. sec., Sept., 1912, and clk. to exec. coun.; col. sec., G. Coast, 18th Aug., 1914; on sp. duty in Togoland, 1st to 28th Sept., 1915; ag. govt., G. Coast on several occasions; gov. and comdr.-in-chief, Sierra Leone, Apr., 1922; gov. and comdr-in-chief, Gold Coast, 1927; capt.-gen. and gov.-in-ch., Jamaica, 1932; resigned, 1934.

SLEEP, CAPT. ARTHUR, B.Sc. (Manchester).—B. 1894; cadet, F.M.S., Feb., 1920; attd. land office, Kelantan, Feb., 1920; passed cadet, Nov., 1921; asst. supt., lands, Kelantan, Mar., 1923; asst. dist. offr., Mar., 1925; dist. offr., Aug., 1926; offr., cls. III, Mar., 1931; 2nd asst. sec. to govt., F.M.S., May, 1931; ag. asst. treas., F.M.S. and state treas., Selangor, May, 1934; offr. cls. II, Mar., 1936.

SLOLEY, SIR HERBERT CECIL, K.C.M.G. (1911); C.M.G. (1905).—Served in C.M.R. in campaigns against Griquas and Moirosi (medal with clasp, 1877-8-9); capt. in native contingent, Basuto war, 1880-1; mentioned in despatches; sub-inspr., Cape police, 1883; ditto, Basutoland, 1884; inspr., 1886; asst. comsnt., Basutoland, 1889 ag. res. comsnr., July to Dec., 1893; govt. sec., 1898; ag. res. comsnr., Dec., 1900; res. comsnr., Sept., 1901; ret., 1926.

SMALL, ALEXANDER SYM., M.A., B.Sc. (Glas.).—B. 1887; ed. Glasgow Univ.; cadet, F.M.S., Jan., 1911; offr., cls. V, sec. to res., N. Sembilan, Mar., 1914; offr., cls. IV, Jan., 1919; offr., cls. III, Jan., 1923; town planning adminstr., K. Lumpur, Dec., 1926; offr., cls. Ia, finan. comsnr. and audr.-gen., Johore, June, 1927; offr., cls. Ia, finan. advr. and treas., F.M.S., Dec., 1930; treas., S.S., June, 1932; col. sec., S.S., Dec., 1935.

SMALL, WILLIAM, M.B.E. (Mily.), ment. in despr.—B. 1885; ed. Univ. of St. Andrews; D.Sc.; botanist, Uganda, 1913; mycologist, 1920;
mycologist, Ceylon, 1926; dir. of agr., Nyassaland, 1930.

SMALLEY, JAMES THORNTON, M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.).—B. 1882; late clinical asst., asst. house surg., out-pat. offr. and house surg., Guy's hosp.; clinical asst., Evelina hosp., London; R.M.O., Colony hosp., Suva, Fiji; D.M.O., Ra; D.M.O. and M.O.H., and port med. offr., Levuka; stip. mag., Levuka, 1910-1913; med. offr., Kowloon and New Territories, Hong Kong, med. offr., Kowloon-Canton rly.; med. and med. offr. in charge, pub. mortuary, Kowloon, 1913; lecturer in Pharmacology and Therapeutics, and examn., physiology, Hong Kong Univ.; J.P., 1919; visiting med. offr., Kwong Wah hospital; med. offr. in charge, Lai Chi Kok branch prison; surg. lieut., Hong Kong Volunteer Corps; med. offr. gov't. civil hosp., 1923; ag. prin. civ. med. offr., Nov., 1927 to Jan., 1928; ag. dep. dir., med. and sanit. services, Feb., 1928 to Feb., 1929; senr. med. offr. and in ch., Kowloon hosp., Jan., 1931.

SMALLWOOD, MARGARET, M.B., B.S., Grad. L.S.T.M. and Hyg. Trin. Coll., Melbourne Univ.—B. 1898; lady med. offr., inf. wel. centre, Ipoh, May, 1924; do., hosp. Ipoh, Nov., 1927; do., women's hosp., K. Kangsar, Dec., 1933 and Nov., 1935; do., hosp. Ipoh, Sept., 1934.

SMALLWOOD, TROMAN NORMAN, J.P.—B. 1892; ed. Shrewsbury (England), Wellington (N.Z.), and privately; war serv., 1914-17; service with Auckland savings bank, 1908-33; joint managing dir., N.Z. mortgage corpn., 1935; joint managing dir., N.Z. state advances corpn., 1936.

SMART, CAPT. ARCHIBALD GULPILH HOLDSWORTH, M.B.E. (Mil.), M.B., Ch.B., D.P.H., D.T.M. & H.—B. 1882; med. offr., i/c quarantine stn., Singapore, May, 1912; attd., govt. lab., Singapore, Jly., 1913; lent to Kedah for anti-cholera work, Jan.-Apr., 1914; asst. health offr., Singapore, June, 1914; on war serv., R.A.M.C., 1915-18; med. offr., S. Kedah, Oct., 1920; health offr., Kedah, Nov., 1921; ar. health offr., Penang, May, 1927; ditto, Perak, May, 1928; State med. and health offr., Selangor and registr.-gen., births and deaths, F.M.S., Jan., 1932; mem., S.S. and F.M.S. med. coun., Feb., 1932; ret.; senr. med. offr., St. Vincent, 1935.

SMART, HAROLD PHILIP.—B. 1899; ed. Michaelhouse Diocesan Sch., Natal, Glen Sch., of Agr., O.F.S. (Farmers' Weekly gold medallist), Transvaal Univ. Coll., Pretoria, (Farmers' Weekly schol.), B. Sc. Agr., Balliol Coll., Oxford, Imp. Coll., Trop. Agr., Trinidad, A.I.C.T.A.; served with R.N.A.S. and R.A.F., 1918-20; lecturer in dairy ing., dept. agr., Union of S. Africa., 1926; agr. offr., Br. Honduras, 1928.

SMART, LESLIE MASON, C.B.E. (1936)—B. 1889; asst. supt., Kenya and Uganda Rly., Apr., 1919 to Mar., 1927; dep. traffic man., Tanganyika rlys., Mar., 1927; gen. man., Gold Coast rly. and hbr. authority, Takoradi hbr., Oct., 1933.

SMART, V. IRVING.—B. 1875; ed. Upper Canada Coll., Toronto; graduated from Queen's Univ.; engaged on surveys for the Dom. govt., 1897-98; ent. rly. serv., 1900; prof., rly. engnr. and oper., McGill Univ., Montreal, 1907-14; sp. engnr., Canadian National Rlys., 1923-28; gen. supt., trans., Western region, C.N.R., 1928-30; dep. min. of rlys. and canals, Dominion of Canada; also govt. dir., Canadian National Rlys., 1930.

SMARTT, FITZPATRICK FORBES PERCY.—Ed. Denstone Coll.; probationer, col. audit dept., July, 1921; asst. audr., Br. Honduras, Oct., 1921; asst. audr., N. Rhodesia, May, 1921; Tanganyika Territory, 1934.

SMIT, DOUGLAS LAING.—B. 1883; obs. serv., 1903; pub. prob., 1912; mag., 1913; sec. for just., Pretoria, 1933; sec. nat., 1934.

SMIT, HAROLD PRINGLE.—B. 1883; Cape civ. serv., Jan., 1901; office of intell., May-Aug., 1902; Transvaal ar., Sept., 1902; ch. clk. to atty.-gen., Transvaal, July, 1908; addl. mag., Beombi, Sept., 1910; war stores comm., 1915; mag., Bloemfontein, Dec., 1915; ch. clk., dept. of just., Dec., 1915; pub. serv., inap., Feb., 1922; sec. for intell., Africas, Apr., 1923; dep. adminstr., May, 1924 and July-Dec., 1928; sec. for land, 1934; contr. and audr.-gen., Nov., 1935.

SMIT, JACOBUS STEPHANUS.—B. 1878; (Dekoratie Trouwe Dienst), Anglo-East African, barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1905; sec. to Gen. Smute as col. sec., Transvaal, 1907; Gen. Botha as premier, Transvaal, 1910; Hon. J. de Villiers as atty.-gen., Transvaal, 1910; asst. mag., Transvaal, 1909; addl. mag., Transvaal, 1910; sec. civ. serv., 1910; resig., 1915; el. mem. Bloemfontein, Union of S. Africa, legis. assm., 1920 and 1924; high commr. for Union of S. Africa, London, 1925; admstr., Transvaal, 1930; chmn., diamond control bd., 1934.

SMITH, LINUT. ARTHUR BERTRAM, F.R.C.S. B. 1889; ed. R. Masonic Sch., Bursary lieut., R.N.R., Oct., 1914; as. lieut., Jan., 1915; served in 8th submarine flotilla, 1914-15; 1st submarine flotilla, 1915-17; Russian Ostend, Anne, 3rd cls. (with swords), 1915; Russian St. Vladimir, 4th cls. (with swords); commanded submarine C 14 (N. Sea), Aug., 1918, and various surrendered submarines, Nov., 1918 to Mar., 1919; St. Dar-es-Salam, Mar., 1919; harbour and lighthouses, Trinidad, Feb., 1926.

SMITH, ALLAN CHALMERS, B.A. (Eng.), B. 1893; ed. Warwick Acad., Bermuda; Schil., and St. John's Coll., Oxford; cadet, Gray's Inn, June, 1920; war serv., South Africa, 1915-18 (three times ment.); pol. mag., W. dist., Bermuda, 1920; M.L.A., 1920; pol. mag., cent. dist., licensing authorities, Oct., 1931; constab., Nigeria, Jan., 1935.

SMITH, A. H. W., M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.P.M. (Univ. of London), M.R.C.P. (Lond.), St. Ann's lunatic asylum, Trinidad, 1924.

SMITH, B. O.—Cler., asst. postmaster, Guiana, Aug., 1898; sec., leave reg., 1900; sec., deptl. salaries gradually promoted to 1st cls. clk., currency comsrs., July, 1923; treas. secretariat, Apr., 1925; accnt., 1926-29; ch. acct., G.P.O., Dec., 1930; 1933-36.

SMITH, CHARLES ROBERT.—B. 1893; Borneo serv., Aug., 1913; asst. postmaster, 1916; mag., 1st cls., Jan., 1918; 2nd cls., 1919; asst. gov't. sec., Oct., 1920; July, 1929; ag. rec., May, 1930; sec., ag. gov't. sec., Mar., 1934; addl. mag., 1934; ag. judge, high ct., June, 1936; judge, high ct., Sept., 1937.

SMITH, CLIVE ALEXANDER.—Ed. Malton Grammar Schl.; R. N. Navy, inspr., Jamaica constab., Dec., 1929; inspr., May, 1930.

SMITH, CUTHBERT, Dip. in Forestry, B. 1890; asst. conserv., forest dept., 1930.
SMITH, HON. DAVID STANLEY, LL.M.—1888; ed. Southland Boys' High Sch., Wellington Coll. and Victoria Univ. Coll. (N.Z.); serv. with N.Z. expd. force, 1917-18; rtrrister, solic., and notary pub. till apptd. judge, Z. sup. ct., 1928; examr. in law, univ. of Z., 1920-27; appointee of U.S.A. as non-tional mem., perm. comm. to settle disputes between U.S.A. and Peru; chmn., native affrs. comm. (N.Z.), 1934; author of "Adoption of children in N.Z." in Journal of Comparative Legislation, Oct., 1921.

SMITH, E. A.—B. 1896; ent. E.I.O., Dec., 1911; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., Dec., 1913; on milly. serv., Dec., 1915 to Jan., 1919; er. offr., 1st Jan., 1920.

SMITH, EDWARD PAUL.—B. 1884; Cape mounted pol., June, 1901; clk. to regt. deeds, Cape Town, 1903; clk. to high sheriff, C.T., 1907; 2nd gr. clk., pub. ser. commn., 1913; on milly. serv.; Great War, 1915-18 (wounded); 1st r. clk., ditto, 1919; 1st gr. clk., treas., 1920; snr. clk., P.S.C., 1922; prin. clk., ditto, 1927; h. clk., ditto, 1930; pub. ser. inspr., 1931; under sec., dept. of commerce and industries, 1935.

SMITH, EMILE HAMEL, L.R.C.P., L.R.C.S., F.P. and S., Glas.—B. 1879; ent. med. serv., Trinidad, Sept., 1909; dist. med. offr., Dec., 1912.

SMITH, ERNEST ALLEN.—B. 1886; war serv., 1914-19; asst. audr., Gold Coast, 1924; audr., Eeward Is., 1927; senr. asst. audr., N. Rhodesia, 1932; ag. audr., 1934; dep. audr., Gold Coast, 1936.

SMITH, ERNEST GARDINER, M.A., LL.B.—Advoc.; prizeman in constiit. law and list; ass't. list. commnr., S. Nigeria, Aug., 1908; ass't. pol. mag., Jan., 1911; 2nd grade mag., Nigeria, Jan., 1914; 1st grade mag., Jan., 1914; transfd. to legal dept., Sept., 1914; ag. solr. gen., Aug., 1920 to Apr., 1921 and Aug., 1921 to Mar., 1922; circuit judge, Ashanti and N. Territories, G. Coast, Aug., 1922; puisne judge, G. Coast, June, 1925; ret., 1931; ch. just., Seychelles, 1935; compiled 1928 edition Laws of Gold Coast, Ashanti, etc.

SMITH, ERNEST JOHN.—B. 1888; ed. E. London Tech. Coll.; milly. serv., Gold Coast Volunteers, 1914-18; asst. acct., constrn., Gold Coast rly., 1920; ch. acct., 1922; dep. ch. constrn. acct., Nigerian rly., 1929; asst. ch. acct., 1930; ch. acct., 1933.

SMITH, FRANCIS EDWARD VINEY, B.Sc. (Hons.)—Ed. Colston's Schl. and Univ., Bristol, 1921; dept. sci. and indust. research, 1921; senr. asst. mycologist, min. of agr. and fisheries, Eng., 1924; gov't. microbiologist, Jamaica, 1927; Jamaica del., Impl. Mycological Confe., and Impl. Meteorological Confe., London, 1929; banana industry ad bd, 1932; ag. dir., agr., 1933; sec., W.I. Fruit and Veg. Confe., 1933; mission, Honduras and Florida on citrus industry, 1933.

SMITH, FREDERIC GORDON, K.C.—B. 1886; ed. Bromsgrove Schl.; solr., Jan., 1909; barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, July, 1921; legal dept., N. Rhodesia, 1913; on active serv. in East Africa with N.R. Police, July, 1915 to July, 1918; held various appts. in legal dept., N. Rhodesia during B.S.A. Co.'s admn., including regt., high ct. etc., and asst. legal adviser and pub. prov.; asst. atty.-gen., Oct., 1924; solr.-gen., Kenya, Sept., 1926; atty.-gen., N. Rhodesia, Apr., 1927; ag. judge, high ct., Sept., 1927 to Mar., 1928 and in 1931; mem., exec. and leg. couns.; atty.-gen., Trinidad, Oct., 1932; puisne judge.

SMITH-FOLLETT, ROBERT REDVERS, B.Sc., A.R.C.S.—B. 1901; ed. Skinners Schl. and Impl. Coll. Sci. and Tech. (B.Sc. hons. chem.); Impl. Col. Trop. Agr., Trinidad, 1925; research asst. to prof., chem. and soil sci., 1927; chemist-ecologist attd. to col. comte., Br. Guiana, 1929; chemist-ecologist, dept. agr., Br. Guiana, 1930.

SMITH, SIR GEORGE, K.C.M.G. (1914), C.M.G. (1911).—B. 1858; entd. war office, Apr., 1878; clk., oh. sec.'s office, Cyprus, Nov., 1879; ch. clk., ditto, 1881; asst. to oh. sec., Dec., 1883; clk., legis. coun., Mar., 1886 to Nov., 1891; commr., Papho, Nov., 1891; regar.-gen. and offl. mem. of legis. coun., June, 1895; as sec., Col. and Ind. Exhib. comte., 1886; sec. to Queen's Jubilee Memorial comte., 1887; pres. mun. commr., Papho, 1892; ag. Br. del. of Evcaf., under convn. with Turkey, Mar., to Nov., 1903; ag. prin. forest offr., 1903, and 1907; ag. dir. of agric., 1904 and 1905; Br. del. of Evcaf., July, 1905; ag. recr.-gen., and ch. collr. of cust., 1905, 1906, 1907 and 1909; col. sec., Mauritius, June, 1910; administered govt., Apr., to Nov., 1911; gov't., Nyassaland, May, 1913; assumed govt., Sept., 1913; ret., Deo., 1923.

SMITH, HAROLD DIGBY.—B. 1889; ed. Otago Boy's High Schl., Dunedin; war serv., 1915-19; joined N.Z. postal dept., 1906; regar., pensions, 1914; asst. commr., pensions, 1929; commr., 1936.

SMITH, HARRY ALSTON.—B. 1886; stock inspr., Basutoland, 1913; sub.-inspr. Basutoland mounted pol., 1919; war serv., 1914-18; inspr., 1930.

SMITH, HARRY LESTER, O.B.E. (1933).—B. 1884; clk., G.P.O., O.R.C., May, 1903; clk., col. sec.'s office, O.R.C., Aug., 1903; clk., gov't. office, O.R.C., 1907; clk., gov'-genl.'s office, Union of S.A., May, 1910; prin. clk., July, 1924; ch. clk., Nov., 1926; ag. sec. to gov'-genl., Oct., 1925 to Jan., 1927; ch. clk., off. of high commr. for S.A., Jan., 1928; sec. Swaziland finan. and econ. comm., 1931-32; ditto, Basutoland, 1934-35; asst. admin. sec., 1934.

SMITH, HUGH MIDDLETON BRICE, M.A.—B. 1884; ed. at Pocklington Schl. and Queen's Coll., Cambridge; asst. res., N. Nigeria Jan., 1909; 2nd cls. dist. offr., Oct., 1917; ag. mag. in 1921 and 1922.

SMITH, JAMES.—B. 1882; stock inspr., Basutoland, 1911; sub.-inspr., Basutoland mounted pol., 1917; inspr., 1926.

SMITH, JAMES DAVID MAXWELL, M.A. (Aberdeen).—B. 1895; cadet, F.M.S., July, 1920; asst. collr., land rev., Lower Perak, Oct., 1920; passed cadet, July, 1922; offr., cls. V, Sept., 1922; asst. sec. to res., Perak, July, 1925; offr., cls. IV., Sept., 1926; offr., cls. III., Sept., 1931; retrenchment offr., F.M.S., May, 1932; ag. legal advr. and judl. commr., Kelantan, Apr., 1934; offr. cls. II., Sept., 1936.

SMITH, JAMES LANDRETH.—B. 1870; draftsman, P.W.D., St. Lucia, July, 1891; draftsman, survey offr., Sept., 1893; warden, and supt. of water-wks. under St. George's town bd., Apr., 1895 to Aug., 1901; chief overseer of roads and works, Grenada, Aug., 1901; asst. supt. of wks., Apr., 1902; commr. of crown lands, June, 1904; survr., crown lands, 1904; ag. supt., wks., June, 1906 to Jan., 1907; supervisor, gov't. cotton ginnery, Oct., 1912; col. engrnr., Oct., 1918 to Aug., 1920; supt., pub. wks., St. Kitts-Nevis, Sept., 1920.
SMITH, JOHN, O.B.E. (1933).—B. 1883; ed. New Vety. Coll., Edinburgh (M.R.C.V.S.), and Liverpool Univ. (D.V.H.); vety. offr., N. Rhodesia, June, 1913; resigned, Apr., 1916; active serv., 1916-19; capt.; reappt., Oct., 1921; ag. ch. vety. offr., Nov., 1921-May, 1922; ch. vety. offr., May, 1922; mem., leg. coun.; ag. sec. for agr., Apr., 1925; J.P.; dir., animal health, Nov., 1929.

SMITH, JOHN NOEL.—B. 1886; ed. at Summer Fields, Oxford, Radley Coll. and Hertford Coll., Oxford; 2nd lieut., 3rd (Rcs.) Batt., Oxford and Bucks. Light Infantry, 1909; seconded for serv. as asst. res., N. Nigeria, Nov., 1910; attd. Nigeria Regt., Cameroons, Mar., 1915; station mag., N. Provs., Mar., 1919; dist. offr., Jan., 1921; ag. sen. res., Sept., 1923.

SMITH, JOSEPH MARO, O.B.E. 1927, M.R.C.V.S.—Vet. inspr., min. of agric., Egypt, 1912-14; lieut., R.A.V.C., 1914; mily. service, 1914-19; major, 1919; ch. vety. offr., Palestine, July, 1920.

SMITH, L. J. D.—B. 1893; ed. Rastrick Grammar Schl.; U.K. cust., 1914-16; mily. serv., 1917-19; aspt. cust., Tanganyika Territory, 1919; senr. supervsr., cust., 1935.

SMITH, LAWRENCE DELPRÉ.—B. 1905; ed. Christ's Hosp., and Hertford Coll., Oxford (class. exhib.); B.A. 1928; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1929; cadet, Tanganyika Territory, 1929; asst. dist. offr., 1931; ag. crown coun., Jan., 1933-Apr., 1934; res. mag., Apr., 1934.

SMITH, LEO ANDREW, A.R.S.M., Assoc. Inst. M.M.—B. 1886; inspr., mines, Perak, June, 1916; asst. warden, mines, June, 1925; sr. inspr., mines, Larut, Feb., 1931; asst. warden, miner, Selangor, Aug., 1932; ditto, Perak, Mar., 1933 and Nov., 1934; ag. warden, mines, Perak, Sept., 1933.

SMITH, LESLIE STEPHEN.—B. 1898; entd. reglary. of friendly societies, 16th Jan., 1914; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., 27th Apr., 1916; on mily. serv., Jan., 1917 to Feb., 1919; trans. to savings bank dept., G.P.O., May, 1919; trans. to C.O., June, 1923; higher grade cler. offr., 1st Mar., 1930.

SMITH, LINDSAY LEE.—B. 1870; ag. clk. to commr., Turks Is., 1894, 1896, 1900, and 1903; confirmed 1st July, 1903; ag. acctnt. and clk. (collr. of customs, postmr., cashier and regiir. of shipping) commr.'s office, June to Sept., 1904, and May to Aug., 1906; acctnt. and clk. (collr. of cust., postmr., cashier, and regiir. of shipping), Jan., 1907; gen. man., savings bank, 1st July, 1907; ag. asst. commr., Dec., 1910 to Jan., 1911, and from Sept., 1912 to Apr., 1913.

SMITH, M.G., M.A.—B. 1904; inspr., schls., Gold Coast, Dec., 1926.

SMITH, NORMAN LOCKHART.—B. 1887; ed. at Sedbergh and Queen's Coll., Oxford (Hastings scholar); B.A. 1910; cadet, Hong Kong, Oct., 1910; ag. asst. dist. offr., (north), 1912; ag. 2nd A.R.G., 1913; J.P. 1913; ag. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1913; ag. 1st asst. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1913; ag. asst. postmr.-gen., 1914; ag. postmr.-gen., 1915; seconded for military service 1916-19; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1919, 1920 and 1923; recd. Chinese order of Wen-hu, 5th cls., 1920; aspt., impts. and expts., 1921; attd. Geneva opium confce., 1923; head of saniy. dept., 1924; P.M.G., Oct., 1928; 2nd asst. col. sec. and dep. clk. of couns., 1930; prin. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., 1931; dir., educn., 1933; sec. Chinese affrs. and mem., exec. and legis. couns., Mar., 1934; O.A.G., Sept., 1935; sec., Chinese affrs. and mem., exec. and leg. couns., Nov., 1935; col. sec., 1936.

SMITH, P. C., M.I.Munic.R. (Lond.)—B. 1875; ed. at Wyggeston boys' schl., Eng.; pupil at Messrs. Keites and Fosbrooks, arks. and smtn. Leicester, for five years, and remained four years as asst.; joined staff of Messrs. Smith and Langley, contrs., Lond.; asst. to Mr. C. I. Mike, M.I.C.E., city engr., Sheffield; town engr., Rainy River, Ont., Can.; town engr., Souris, Manitoba, 1911; dist. engr Berbice, Br. Guiana, Aug., 1915.

SMITH, REGINALD HOPKINSON, O.B.E. (C.B.E.)—B. 1898; ed. Chatham House, Banbury; served in the Royal Naval Divn., Oct. to Dec., 1914; H.A.C. Oct., 1915 to Oct., 1917; Irish Army R. of O., Nov., 1917 to Aug., 1919; Field Force, July, 1918 to July, 1919; dist. offr., Somaliland, July, 1919.

SMITH, ROBERT KNOWLTON, LL.B., K.C.—B. 1887; ed. St. Francois Xavier Univ., Antwerp, N.S.; grad. Dalhouise Law Schl.; admitt. Nova Scotia bar, Mar., 1911; K.C., Jan., 1925; crown procs., Cumberland County, N.S. Aug., Oct., 1925; mayor, Amherst, 1923; el. to H.d. Canada, Oct., 1925, re-elec. at g.e., 1926; dep. min. of marine, Aug., 1935.

SMITH, SIDNEY W.—B. 1902; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., C.O., Oct., 1919; asst. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; higher grade cler. el. 29th Oct., 1930.

SMITH, STEPHEN HENRY, C.B.E. (1929). F.A. Ins. H.S.—B. 1865; ed. Grafton Superior Fire Sch.; inspr., continuation schls., N. S. W., June, 1912; asst. under sec., educn., dep. N.S.W., June, 1920; dir., educn., N.S.W., 1925.

SMITH, STEPHEN JOHN.—B. 1887; N.Z. sec. and tel. dept., 1903; internal affrs. dept., 1903; sec., Samoa adminstr., 1915; ch. clk., exec. affrs. dept., 1920-30; ch. clk., Cook Is. 1920-28; sec., 1928.

SMITH, TRAFFORD, M.A.—B. 1912; ed. Boys Schl., Leicester and Trinity Coll., Cambridge, 1930-34 (state schl., senr. schl., Jeston Exh.), B.A., 1933 (1st cls. pts. I and II mod. and languages trip); apptd., after compet. exam., asst. prin., C.O., 1935.

SMITH, WILLIAM FORGAN, M.L.A. (Queensland).—B. and ed. in Scotland; M.L.A. (Queensland) since 1915; successively min. without folio, sec. for pub. wks. and sec. for agr. affs.; stock; premier and treas., June, 1932.

SMITH, WILLIAM HARDEN, B.A., M.R.C.I., B.A.O. (T.C.D.), L.M. (Rot.), I.F.R. (R.C.P. and S.I.), D.T.M. (Calcutta).—ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; surg. sub-lieut., R.N.V.R., 1914; med. offr., Zanzibar, Nov., 1925; ag. D.D.S. on various occasions, 1930-33; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1935.

SMITH, WILLIAM HUMPHREY.—B. 1879; ed. Uppingham and Jesus Coll., Camb., Rustschuk, 1897; Abbott univ. schol., 1899; B.A., 1st class, tripso, pt. I, 1901; 2nd cls. pt. II, histor., 1902; clk., col. audit branch, exchequer and audit dept., Dec., 1903; asst. audr., Nyassaland, Oct., 1904; audr., N. Nigeria, Feb., 1910; asst. exchequer and audit dept., Aug., 1910; audr., Seychelles, Mar., 1911; 1st divn. clk. (2nd cls. col. audit dept., Oct., 1912; on mil. serv., 1914; capt., K.O.Y.L.I., Jan., 1915; wounded Mar., 1917; relinquished commn. owing to wounds and returned to col. audit dept., Sept., 1918; audr., Uganda, Dec., 1923; audr., Kenya, 1927.

SMITH, WILLIAM RAMSAY.—D.Sc., M.I.M.S., Edin.; chmn. cent. bd. of health, exec. vaccination offr., and inspr. of anatomy,
stralia, 1899-1903; chmn., cent. bd. of health
coroner, 1903-29; author of several medical
scientific works.

MUTS, GEN. THE RIGHT HON. J. C., P.C.
(7), C.H., K.C.—B. 1870; ed. at Victoria
mill., Stellenbosch; B.A., Cape Univ., 1891;
scholar at Christ's Coll., Camb.; double
law trips, 1894; barrister, Cape Col.;
attorney, S. African Republic, 1895; served
Boer forces during S. African war, and was
cmd. of Boer forces in Cape Col. during the
later part of the campaign; mem. of head
of Het Volk; col. sec., Transvaal, 1907;
mem. of Imp. Conf. on Naval and Military
defence, 1909; min. of finance and defence,
of S. Africa, 1912; min. of defence, 1915;
command of troops in E. Africa, 1916; mem.
British war cabinet; represented S. Africa at
conf. at Paris, 1919; prime min. and
min. of native affrs., Union of S. Africa, 1919-24;
P. for Standerton, 1924; leader, opposition,
1924-33; pres., Br. Assn. for Advancement of
science, 1931; min. of just. and dep. prime min.,
allition govt., 1933; leader, S. African delega-
tion, World Economic Conf., 1933.

SMYLY, SIR PHILIP CRAMPTON, KT. BACH.
(905).—B. 1866; ed. at Trin. Coll., Dub., B.A.,
L.B.; called to the bar, King's Inn, Dub., 1888;
L.D., 1891; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1892;
queen's advoc., S. Leone, 1895; atty.-gen., 1896;
just., S. Leone, 1901; ch. just., Gold Coast,
1911; ret., 1929.

SNELL, EDWARD WALTER.—B. 1879; asst.
office, Kingwilliamstown, Mar., 1900; asst.
P.O., Cape Town, Nov., 1900; clk., accts.
ranch, July, 1903; 1st cls. clk., Apr., 1912;
income tax office, Pretoria, Sept., 1914; senr.
clk., income tax office, Cape Town, July, 1915;
senior clk., rev. office, Johannesburg, Mar.,
918; prin. clk., ditto, Jan., 1921; clk., ch.
accts, income tax, head office, inland rev. dept.,
Pretoria, Aug., 1921; asst. compt. inland rev.,
Sept., 1929.

SNELLING, ARTHUR WENDELL.—B. 1914;
d. Ackworth Schol. and Univ. Coll., London;
Sc. (economics) lst. cls. hons., 1934; study
group sec., Royal Inst. of Internat. Affairs., 1934-
16; appl. after compet. exam., asst. prin., D.O.,
Oct., 1936.

SNYMAN, NICOLAAS.—Prof. asst. to survr.,
O.F.S., 1920; survr.-gen., O.F.S., Dec.,
1931; ditto, Natal, May, 1934.

SOLLIS, CLIFFORD GEORGE, M.A.—B. 1895;
ed. Bristol Grammar Schol. and St. John's Coll.,
Oxford; asst. mast., Bukit Zahrah Sch., Johore
Bahru, Dec., 1920; ag. inspr., schls., Pahang,
Oct., 1925; do., Penang, Mar., 1928; asst. educn.,
Kedah, Dec., 1930; inspr., schla., Selangor,
Aug., 1931.

SOLOMON, SAUL.—B. 1875; ed. Bedford
Grammar Schol. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; M.A.;
called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1900; K.C., Union
of S. Africa, 1919; judge, sup. ct., Transvaal prov.
divn., 1927.

SOMASUNTHARAM, KANDIAH.—B. 1897;
cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; attd.,
Kalutara kach., Dec., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala
kach., Jan., 1922; ditto, Colomba Kach., Dec.,
1922; office asst. to rubber contr., Mar., 1923;
office asst., Galle kach., Aug., 1926; 5th asst.
col. sec., Nov., 1926; 4th asst. col. sec., May,
1928; addnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Jan.,
1929; addnl. asst. contr., rev., Nov., 1929; asst.
govt. agt., Kurunegala, July, 1931; dist. judge,
Kegalla, July, 1932; sec., min. for lab., industry
and commerce, June, 1933; dep. contr., lab.,
May, 1934; contr., finance and supply, Jan., 1936.

SOMERS (6TH BARON, CR. 1784), ARTHUR
HERBERT SOMERS COCKS, K.C.M.G. (1926),
D.S.O. (1919), M.C. (1917).—B. 1887; ed. Charterhouse
and New Coll., Oxford; serv. in Great
War, 1914-19; capt., 1st Life Guards, 1914; lieut.-col.,
Tank Corps, 1918-19; ret., 1922; a lord in
waiting in ordinary to the King, 1924; gov'r. of
Victoria, 1926-31.

SOMERS, CECIL GEORGE.—B. 1896; served
Dardanelles and E. Mediterranean with H.M.
Transporta, 1914-18; gov't. pilot, Kenya, 1924;
asst. port offr., Zanzibar, 1929; ag. port offr.,
on various occasions, 1929-35.

SOIFER, MAJOR EDWARD JOSEPH, (R. of O.).
V.D.—B. 1889; engng. acct., F.M.S. Rly., Sept.,
1923; asst. acct., Jan., 1925 and June, 1931;
fincl. offr., engng. dept., July, 1928; do., gr. I.,
Sept., 1928; rev. acctnt., Aug., 1935.

SOPER, JOHN ROBERT PHILPOTT, B.A.
(hons.), Cantab.—B. 1904; ed. Taunbridge Schol.
and Pembroke Coll., Cambridge (schol.); head-
master, agrl. prim. schl., Zanzibar, Sept., 1926;
seconded for duty as agrl. offr., 1926; agrl. offr.,
1928; do., S.S. and F.M.S., 1936.

SOUTH, FRANCIS WILTON, M.A. (Cantab.)—
B. 1886; ed. Marlborough Coll., and Emmanuel
Coll., Cambridge; mycologist and lect. in agrl.
sci., Imp. dept. of agrf. for W. Indies, Mar., 1909;
ch. agrl. inspr., agrl. dept., F.M.S., May, 1913;
ch. agrl. field offr., Nov., 1924; ag. sec. for agrl.,
S.S. and F.M.S., for various periods 1927-31; rep.
of Malaya at mycological conf., in Lond., Sept.,
1929; ag. dir., agrl., S.S. and F.M.S. for various
periods, 1929 and 1931-32.

SOUTHBOURGH, 1ST BARON (creat.
1917), RT. HON. SIR FRANCIS JOHN STEPHENS
HOPWOOD, P.C. (1912), G.C.B. (1916), G.C.M.G.
(1908), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1906), C.B.
(1895), C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1860; ed. at Louth by
Canon W. W Hopwood; admitted a solr., 1882;
asst. law clk., B. of T., 1885-1888; asst. solr.,
1888-1892; priv. sec. to pres. of B. of T. 1892; sec.,
fly dept., 1892-1901; perm. sec., 1901; perm.
under-sec. of S. for the colonies, 1907-1910;
employed on different occasions upon offl. missions
to U.S.A., Canada, and Newfoundland; Brit.
deleg. to internat. rly. congress in London, 1895;
and in Paris, 1900; hon. sec. to chmn. of select
comte. of H. of C. on Jamaica raid, 1897;
mem. of London traffic coman., 1903; visited
S. Africa as mem. of Transvaal and O.R.C.
constitutions coman., 1906; mem. of comans. on
canals and waterways, 1906; and on ocean
freights and shipping "rings," 1906; accom-
panied H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit
to Quebec, 1908; mem. of Royal coman. on
electoral reform, 1909; reg'ar. of the Order of St.
Michael and St. George, 1907-1909; sec. of the
Order, 1909-1911; accompanied H.R.H. the
Duke of Connaught on his visit to S. Africa in
connection with the opening of the first parlmt.
of the Union of S. Africa, 1910; vice-chmn. of
the Development coman., 1910; specially apptd.
to act as under-sec. of state for the colonies
during the period of the Imperial Conf., 1911;
additional civil lord of the Admiralty, Jan.,
1912; sec. to the Irish Convention, 1917.

SOUTHORN, SIR (WILFRID) THOMAS, K.B.E.
(1933), C.M.G.(1927).—B. 1879; ed. Warwick schol.
and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (M.A.); hon.
LL.D. (Hong Kong Univ.) 1936; cadet, Ceylon
civ. ser., Nov., 1903; off. asst. to govt. agt.,
N. Prov., Oct. 1904; N.C. Prov., May, 1905; dist.
judge, Tangalla, Apr., 1907; landing survr., customa, Colombo, July, 1909; astt. govt. agt., Matale, Nov., 1911; priv. sec. to gov., Aug., 1914; dep. collr. of customs and landing survr., Colombo, Sept., 1915; 2nd astt. col. sec., Dec., 1919; prin. astt. col. sec., July, 1920; prin. collr., cust. and chmn., Colombo port commn., Dec., 1923; mem., leg. coun., 1923 and exec. coun., 1925; col. sec., Hong Kong, May, 1926; O.A.G., for various periods, 1927-35; gov. and commdr-in-ch., Gambia, Oct., 1936.

SPAFFORD, H. H., B.A.—B. 1899; mily. serv., France, 1917-18; demob., 1921; inspr., schls., Gold Coast, Jan., 1928.

SPARROW, HERBERT ROBERT, A.M.I.E.E.—B. 1889; astt. elec. engrnr., F.M.S., Mar., 1920; elec. engrnr., K. Lumpur, Sept., 1927; ag. dep. ch. elec. engrnr. and inspr. in addn., various periods, 1928-31; ag. ch. elec. engrnr. and inspr., F.M.S., June, 1934.

SPARROW, WILLIAM LABARTE.—B. 1904; pol. probationer, Nov., 1924; astt. supt., pol., Hong Kong, 1927; seconded to Weihaiwei as junr. dist. offr., Jan., 1928; passed in Mandarin and Cantonese; attd. Punjab pol., 1931-2; passed in Urdu, 1932; ag. supt., pol., 1936.

SPEED, SIR EDWIN ARNEY, KT. BACH. (1911).—M.A.; LL.B.; B. 1869; ed. at Rugby, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; major scholar and senior exhibtr., Rugby schl.; scholar and prizeman of Trin. Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. clas. tripso, 1890; 2nd cls. law tripso, Part I., 1891; called to the bar, Inner Temple, June, 1893; dist. comnrr., G. Coast, 1899; atty.-gen., Lagos, 1900; edited a revised edition of Lagos laws, 1901; has acted on numerous occasions as ch. just. and also as col. sec., from Jan., 1905, to Mar., 1906; atty.-gen., S. Nigeria, May, 1906; edited revised edtn. of laws of S. Nigeria, 1907; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1908; retired.

SPEIRS, R. C., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), D.T.M. (Liv.)—B. 1901; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1925.

STRACHEY, SIR CHARLES, K.C.M.G. (1926), C.B. (1920).—B. 1862; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. jun. clk., F.C., 2nd Apr., 1885; 1st cl. jun. clk., 1st May, 1885; sec. Uganda rly. comtee., 10th Sept., 1895; 1st cl. clk., C.O., 20th Nov., 1898; prin. clk., 1st Jan., 1907; delegate on Anglo-German Boundary Conf. (Yola-Chad), Mar., 1906; ditto, Anglo-French (Niger-Chad), May, 1906; ditto, Anglo-German (Yola to sea), Oct., 1909; mem., W. African lands comtee., 1912; plenipotentiary at Brussels Internat. Liquor Conf., 1912; travelled in Nigeria, 1914; mem., Br. delegation, Paris Peace Conf., Jan. to Sept., 1919; Br. rep. on internat. comtees, for preparation of conventions on (1) African liquor traffic, (2) arms traffic, (3) revision of Berlin and Brussels Acts, signed at St. Germain, 10th Sept., 1919; ast. sec., 1st Apr., 1920; ast. under sec. of state, 12th Dec., 1924; ret., Sept., 1927.

STRADBROKE, (3rd EARL OF) (cr. 1821).

GEORGE EDWARD JOHN MOWBRAY ROUS, BARON ROUS (cr. 1796), VISCOUNT DUNWICH (cr. 1821), K.C.M.G. (1920), C.B. (1904), C.V.O., A.D.C., D.L., J.P.—B. 1862; ed. Harrow and Cambridge; col., 1st Norfolk Royal Garrison Art. Volunteers, 1883-1908; col., 3rd (howitzer) brig., E. Anglian divn., R.F.A., 1908-17; col., 272nd brigade, R.F.A., Jan. to Nov., 1917; gov., Victoria, 1920-26.

STRAHAN, FRANK, C.V.O., C.B.E., B.A., LL.B.—Sec., prime min's. dept., C'wealth of Australia; sec., Australian delegn. to the Imp. conf., 1923; govt. dir., Amalgamated Wireless...
(A/asia) Ltd.; sec., Br. Australian and N. Z. Antarctic research expedit.

STRAHAN, KENNETH CYPRIAN.—B. 1880; ed. King's Schl., Canterbury and King's Coll., Cambridge; Ceylon govt. rly., 1908-15; R.A.S.C.M.T., 1915; capt., G.H.Q., Inspection Branch, 1917; ment. in desps.; ch. mech. engr., Tanganyika rly., 1920; ch. mech. engr., Kenya and Uganda rly. and harbrs., 1930.

STRATFORD, JAMES.—B. 1869; ed. St. Aidan's Coll., Grahamstown, Cape Colony and Exeter Coll., Oxford; M.A., B.C.L., Oxon; mem., Inner Temple; called to the bar, England, 1898; Transvaal, 1902; practised, Johannesburg; K.C., 1912; judge, sup. ct., Transvaal prov. division, 1st March, 1921; judge of appeal, 1927.

STREAK, M. J.—B. 1879; ed. Grey Coll., Bloemfontein; C.S., L.L.B.; asst. mag., Jacobsdal, 1900; Hoopstad, 1903; Heilbron, 1904; Senekal, 1908; Harrismith, 1913; mag., Bothaville, 1916; addnl. mag., Bloemfontein, 1919; mag. and mining conn., Namakgualand, 1928; addl. mag., Pretoria, 1929; mag., Ermelo, 1931; 1st civ. mag., Johannesburg, 1932; mag., Pt. Elizabeth, Mar., 1936; do., Pietermaritzburg, Oct., 1936.

STREET, SIR PHILIP WHISTLER, K.C.M.G. (1928).—B. 1863; puisne judge, N.S. Wales; judge in bankruptcy and probate jurisdictions, Feb., 1907; ch. just., 1925; lieut.-gov., 1930.

STRICKLAND, 1st BARON (cr. 1928), SIR GERALD STRICKLAND, COUNT DELLA CATENA, G.C.M.G. (1913), K.C.M.G. (1897), C.M.G. (1889).—B. 1861; ed. Oscott Coll., Birmingham; lieut. C.U.R.V.; and elected mem. coun. of govt., Malta, 1886; B.A. and L.L.B., Trin. Coll., Camb., honours law tripes; attended col. conf., 1887, on behalf of Malta; called to the bar, Inn. Temp., and pres. cholera comsn., Malta, 1887; thanked by govt. for services in negotiations with the Holy See; unoffic. mem., ex. coun., and ag. asst. sec. to govt., 1888; vice-pres., bd. of health, pres. comte. of privileges, ch. sec. to govt., and major, Royal Malta militia, which he established, 1889; re-organized Malta rly., 1891; planned breakwater, 1894; pres., coun. of Malta univ., 1900; chmn., mil. and civ. drainage bd.; mem. comte. on Malta naval reserves; gov. and comdr-in-chief, Leeward Is., 1902; estab. central factories for sugar and cotton in Antigua, 1903; gov., Tasmania, 23rd July, 1904; read scientific papers as pres. of Royal Society, 1904; gov., W. Australia, 6th Apr., 1904; mem. of W. Aust. Inst. of engrns.; gov., New South Wales, 25th Nov., 1912; assumed govt., 14th Mar., 1913; ex-officio gov. of Norfolk Is., 1913-14; codified the laws of Norfolk Is., and negotiated the transfer of the dependency to the Commonwealth; hon. col., 86th W. Australia Infantry Regt.; mem. of Inst. of local govt. engrns., N.S. Wales; held dormant comsn. to administer C. of A. in absence of gov.-gen.; retired, 1917; prime min. of Malta, 1927.

STRINGER, HON. SIR THOMAS WALTER, K.T. BACH. (1928).—B. 1855; ed. high schl., Christchurch, New Zealand; barrister and solr.; K.C., 1908; judge of the sup. ct., New Zealand, 1914-27.

STRONACH, JOHN CLARK, B.A., B.A.I.—B. 1887; ed. St. Andrews Coll., Dublin, Dublin Univ. and Eng. Sch. T.C.D.; asst. engr., Indian pub. wks., 1911; exec. engr., 1919; New Delhi, 1913-26; seconded to Kenya as supl., 1926-29; transf. Kenya, 1930; ag. dir., P.W., 1930 and 1931, 1936.

STRONG, ERNEST EDWARD.—B. 1855; inspr., Basutoland, 1912; sub-insp., mounted pol., 1915; inspr., 1928.

STRONGE, SIR HERBERT (cr. 1919), K.C. (1930), K.C., Ireland.—B. 1875; ed. Schl., and Trin Coll., Dublin; priv. tutor English literature; B.A.; called to King's Inn, Dublin, 1900; joined N.E. July, 1901; stip. mag., Bahamas, 1911; adm. July to Aug., 1914, Sept. to Nov., 1914; May to Sept., 1915; also acted as chief Jan., 1915; chief just. Tonga, 1916; of Tongan govt. for services in 1916; seconded for sup. duty as pres. of com., 1921; ch. just., Leeward Is., 1925; Cyprus, 1931.

STROTHER-STEWART, ROGER B.C.L., B.LITT., Durham Univ., Grademan.—Admitted solr., sup. ct., 1906; the Tynemouth R.G.A. (T.F.), 1914; gen. offr. commdg. Tyne garrison intelligence offr., Tyne garrison, 1919; for valuable services; asst. commdg. authority, Tyne garrison, 1919-20; bar, Inner Temple, 1919; maj. R.O., 1919-27; M.P. for Swindon, 1923-24; mag., county of Victoria, Apr., 1927; temp. asst. legal adviser to Dec., 1929; legal adviser to 2nd Jan., 1930; mem., privy and nomin. coun. of health; examt. in hist. and hist., Univ. of Malta; chmn., enquiry into motor transport, 1930-32; July-Aug., 1932; chmn., traffic commission, 1930-32; chmn., trade union commission, 1932; puisne judge, Gold Coast, 1932; just., Oct. Nov., 1935.

STUART, REV. CYRIL EDGAR, M.A.—ed. Dulwich Coll., Repton and S. and Ridley Hall, Cambridge; B.A., 1920; milv. serv., 1914-19, Saloon deacon, 1920; priest, 1921; curate, Hemdy Rise, 1920; chaplain at Hall, Cambridge, 1920-24; chaplain Achimota, Gold Coast, 1925.

STUBBS, CAPT. EDWARD (1881); ent. R.N., 1885; lieut. (temp.), 1903; commdr., 1916; squadron First Battle Squadron, 1920-22; harbmr., Portsmouth, 1923-25; H.M.S. "Agamemnon" (1925-27); capt., Mar., 1927; master att., Apr., 1927.

STUBBS, SIR REGINALD EDWARD (1928), K.C.M.G. (1919), C.M.G. (1876); ed. at Radley and Coln. Oxford (exhibitioner); 1st cl. lit. hum., 1897; lat cl. lit. hum., 1899; (1920); apptd., after compet., C.O., Jan., 1900; ag. 1st cls. clk., Dec., 1910; 1st cls. clk., Dec., 1910; F.M.S. and Hong Kong to inst. of revision of civ. ser. salary list of West African lands comm., Ceylon, Jan., 1913; O.A.G., Dec., 1915 to Apr., 1916; 1918; gov., Hong Kong; assumed govt., 30th Sept., Rising Sun of Japan, 1st cls. clk., Hong Kong, 1926; hon. (temp.) Coll., Oxford, 1926; capt., Jamaica, 1926; gov. and comm., Dec., 1932, do., Ceylon.
DOMINIONS OFFICE AND COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

List, 1910-1912; edited "Lucas' Historical Geography of the British Colonies" vol. i., 2nd ed., 1906.

TUBINGTON, ROBERT ALAN, P.A.S.I.—B. 3; ed. Cranleigh Sch.; surv. prob., F.M.S.; 2; asst. supt., surveys, 1919; ag. supt., rev. surveys, Pahang, 1928; Selangor, 1929; supt., land surveys, Pahang, 1930; do., Selangor, 1933; ag. senr. do., Perak, Dec., 1934.

TUCKEY, REGINALD ROBERT, C.M.G. (1932).—I.A.; pub. actuary, S. Australia, 1914; under ass., since 1923.

TUPART, SIR ROBERT FREDERIC, KT. BACH. (14).—B. 1857; ed., priv. schl.; Upper Can.; ent. Can. meteorological serv., Nov., 1872; some years was sen. inspr. and probability Toronto observ.; in charge of ch. station, Dawson's Straits, 1884-85; supt. and dir., meteorological serv. of Dom. and of magnetic observ., in Dec., 1894; fellow, Royal Soc., Can., 1901; s., Royal Astron. Soc., Can., 1902-03; pres. yal Can. Inst., 1906-07; mem., internat. theological comtee., 1907 and 1919; pres., St. George's Soc., Toronto, 1919-20; ret., 1929.

STURDY, DONALD, B.A.—B. 1905; ed. Sherborne and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; agril. course, 21-26; B.A., 1926; dist. agril. offr., Tanganyika territory, Dec., 1926.

STURGES, ROBERT SIMON MANSFIELD, O.B.E. (29).—B. 1893; ed. Radley and Christ Ch.; st. pol. offr., Iraq civ. admin., Apr., 1920; terial oriental sec. to high commr., Iraq, Feb., 21; asst. sec., Apr., 1921; polit. sec., Oct., 24.

*STURROCK, Sir JOHN CHRISTIAN RAMSAY, B. Bach. (1934), C.M.G. (1927), M.A. (Oxon.).—1875; ed. Charterhouse and Balliol Coll., Oxford; tutor to H.H. the Kabaka of Buganda, ar., 1905; dist. commr., Uganda Prot., Aug., 14; prov. commr., June, 1921; ag. ch. sec., Jan., 1924; res. commr., Basutoland, 1926; ret., 1935.

STUTTAFORD, RICHARD.—B. 1870; M.P. for Newlands, Union of S. Africa from 1924; in. without portfolio, 1933.

SUDSBURY, EDWIN RONALD, M.A. (Oxon.).—1897; on mily. serv., Jan., 1916; cadet, Ceylon v. serv., Aug., 1921; attd. to Kurunegala Kach., sept., 1921; attd., Nuwara Eliya kach., Nov., 1921; gtr. office asst. to govt. agt., C. Prov., Jan., 1925; pte. sec. and A.D.C. to O.A.G., Apr., 1925; fice asst. to govt. agt., Cent. Prov., Feb., 1927; ast. govt. agt., Kandy, Nov., 1928; on sp. duties connexion with new constitution, Jan., 1930; admstve. sec., income tax dept., June, 1932; lk., bd. of review in addn.; admstve. sec., amalgamated depts., of income tax, estate duty nd stamps, and clk., bd. of review, Oct., 1933.

SUKUNA, JOSEVA LALABALAVU VANAALI, J.A. (Oxon.), Barrister-at-Law, Middle Temple.—d. Wanganui, N.Z. and Wadham Coll., Oxford; held various appts., col. secretariat and native offices, Fiji 1907-12; served in France with the Foreign Legion and awarded the Mily. Med., 1914-16; ag. asst. sec. for native affrs. and aide-de-camp, 1916; cadet, Fiji, 1917; served in France with Fiji Labour Corps, 1917-18; called to bar, 1921; passed cadet, 1921; native lands commr., 1922; ag. dep. registr., sup. ct., 1922; ast. commr. for Fiji, Br. Empire Exhib., 1924; ag. chmn. native lands commr., 1927; dist. commr., Lau, 1932; nom. native mem., leg. coun., 1932.

SULLIVAN, HON. DANIEL GILES, J.P.—B. 1882; ed. Marist Bros. schl., Christchurch, N.Z.; mem., N.Z. H. of R. since 1919; min. of rly. and min. of industries and commerce, 1935.

SULLIVAN, JOHN.—Engr., marine dept., Nigeria, 1910; Cameroons Expedy. Force, 1914-16; engr., adviser to French at Duala, 1916; supt. engr., marine dept., 1927.

SULLIVAN, JOHN ALEXANDER, K.C., B.C., B.A., LL.B.—B. 1879; capt., R. of O. barrister-sol. and atty., former vice-pres., Montreal bar; mem., gen. coun., Quebec bar; mem., bd. of exam., do.; el. to H. of C., Canada, July, 1930; dep. P.M.G., Aug., 1935.

SUMMERS, WALTER LLOYD.—B. 1870; entd. crown lands off., S. Aust., July, 1887; clk., agri. off., May, 1892; chief clk., July, 1902; ag. sec. to min. of agri., Feb., 1910; sec. to ditto, July, 1911; also sec. to min. of industry and sec. to min. of marine, 1915.

SUMNER, JAMES A. W.—B. 1903; entd. L.P.S. (Inland Rev.), May, 1919; apptd. after compet. exam. cler. offr., London telephone serv., Apr., 1921; transfld., C.O., Oct., 1923.

SURRIDGE, BREWSTER JOSEPH.—B. 1894; ed. Felsted Coll., and Downing Coll., Cambridge; B.A.; served, N. Lancs. regt., 1914-17; ast. sec. ch. secs. office, Cyprus, Mar., 1918; passed exam. in mod. Greek, Nov., 1918; ag. ch. ast. sec., Jan. to Apr., 1919; local const., police, Apr., 1919; ag. commr., Larnaca, June, 1919; ag. A.D.C., July, 1920; ag. ast. sec., Oct., 1920; passed exam. in Turkish, Aug., 1922; ag. commr., Aug., 1922; ag. ast. sec., Sept., 1922; commr., Jan., 1924; admstve. offr.; commr. and registrar, co-op. and co-op. credit socs., Jan., 1933; registrar, co-op. and co-op. credit socs., Mar., 1936.

SURRIDGE, ERNEST REX EDWARD.—B. 1899; ed. Felsted and St. John's Coll., Oxford; mod. hist. (hon.); B.A., 1922; lieut. 7th Batt., The Duke of Cornwall's Light Infy., 1917-20; France and Germany; ast. dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1924; seconded to secretariat, 1925-28; aide-de-camp and pte. sec. to ag. gov., 1928; seconded to C.O. as ast. prin., Sept., 1930-Feb., 1933; seconded to secretariat, 1933; ag. dep. ch. sec., 1933; ast. ch. sec., 1936.

SURVEYER, HON. EDOUARD FABRE.—B. 1875; ed., Ste. Marie Coll., McGill and Laval Univs.; called to bar, 1896; vice-pres., Jun. Bar Assoc., 1902-03; pres., 1903-04; mem. of coun. of Quebec bar, 1904-05; lectr., law, McGill Univ. since 1905; judge, superior ct., Quebec, 1st Jan., 1920; edr. of practice repts., Que., since 1898; also of pocket eds. of civ. code and code of civ. procedure (the latter in both languages); pres., Can. Club, Montreal, 1909-10; vice-pres., l'alliance Francaise, Montreal.

SUTCLIFFE, MAJOR A. W., D.S.O., M.C., B.Sc. (Durham).—Ast. dist. commr., Kenya, May, 1920.

SUTHERLAND, HON. DONALD MATHESON, P.C. (Can.), M.B., D.S.O.—B. 1879; 1st el. to rep. S. Oxford in Ont. legis., g. e., May, 1902; re-el., g. e., Jan., 1905; dir., colonization and immigr., Ontario, Mar., 1909; el. at g. e., Dec., 1921; re-elect., g. e., 1925 and 1930; min. of national defence in Bennett cabinet, Aug., 1930; re-elect. by acc. after assuming office, Aug., 1930.

SUTTON, G., A.M.C.T.—B. 1902; ed. Accrington Grammar Schl. and Tech. Schl., Manchester Coll. of Technology; mast., Accra tech. schl., Gold Coast, June, 1927.

SUTTON, GEORGE GERHARD, K.C., LL.B.—B. 1880; ed. Dale Coll., King William's Town, Union of S. Africa, Manchester Grammar Schl. and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; called to bar,
Middle Temple, June, 1903; admitted to bar, sup. ct., Cape Town, Oct., 1903; K.C. for Union of S. Africa, Sept., 1921; ag. judge, Cape prov. divn., on various occasions, 1922-28; judge, Cape prov. divn., Feb., 1929.

SWABEY, CHRISTOPHER.—B. 1906; ed. Winchester Coll. and Edinburgh Univ.; Younger silver med. for forestry, 1927; B.Sc. (forestry), 1928; asst. conservator, forests, Trinidad, 1928.

SWAINE, CAPT. DAVID RICHARD, M.A. (Wales).—B. 1889; asst. mast., Penang Free Schl., Sept., 1913; on milly. serv., 1915-19; twice men. in desps., M.C., asst. mast., Penang Free Schl., Feb., 1920; sr. normal instr., Penang, in addn., Mar., 1920; headmast., Northam Rd. Sch., Dec., 1924; European mast., cl. IB; prin., King Edward VII Schl., Taiping Sept., 1929; ag. ch. inspr., Eng. schls., S.S. & F.M.S., Sept., 1934; prin., Raffles Inst., S'pore, June, 1935; asupt., educn., Johore, Oct., 1935.

SWAN, GEORGE.—R. 1897; asst. govt. marine surv., Hong Kong, 1924; Hong Kong del. to safety of life at sea conf., Simla, 1931.

SWAYNE, COL. SIR ERIC JOHN EAGLES, K.C.M.G. (1910), C.B. (mil.) (1904); grand offr. of order of the Crown of Italy (1905).—B. 1863; ed. at naval coll., Gosport, and abroad; R.M.C., Sandhurst, 1882; end. Welsh regt., 1883; Bengal staff corps, 1884; adjut., 1888; capt., 1894; local lieut.-col., 1900; brevet lieut.-col., 1901; brevet-col., 1903; temp. brig.-gen., 1903-1906; retired from army, 1906; served with Burma expdn., 1883-86 (medal with clasp); intell. offr., Hukong Valley reconnaissance; in command of advanced base exploration, Turong River and Sing P'ho country, Nov., 1895 to Moh., 1896 (McGregor medal); exploration to Somaliland, Feb. to July, 1891 (thanked by resolution of Bombay govt., and appreciation by govt. of India); Gildessas affair on Abyssinian frontier, 1892 (commendation by resolution of Bombay govt.); engaged on delimitation of internat. frontier between French and British Somaliland, 1892; served for five years on intell. staff, India, as staff-capt. and D.A.Q.M.G.; apptd. 2nd-in-command, Uganda Rifles, on active serv. in Jubaland, E. Africa (medal with clasp); on active serv. in Uganda, 1899; selected to command Somaliland police force, 1900; raised and organised levies, and commanded expeditionary force in Somaliland, Nov., 1900; defeated and routed Mullah (ment. in desps., medal with clasp, brevet lt.-col., thanked by govt.); organised 6th Batt. Uganda Rifles, second expdn., 1901; again defeated Mullah (C.B., ment. in desps.); apptd. comsnr., consul-gen. and comdr.-in-chief, Somaliland Prot., and judge of its high court, Apr., 1902; on special duty in Egypt, 1904; arranged evacuation of Somaliland, and organised control of tribes; British deleg. to conference with Italian deleg. at Lyons in connection with agreement with Italy respecting Somaliland; gov. and comdr.-in-chief, British Honduras, 1906-13; spec. duty to Canada, with reference to Indian labour (thanked by govt. of India) 1908; spec. duty to Mexico, 1909.

SWEET ESCOTT, Sir E. B., K.C.M.G. (1904), C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1857; ed. Somersetshire Coll., Bath, and at Balliol Coll., Oxon; exhibitioner, Wores. Coll., Oxon, June, 1876; 2ndclass classical mods., June, 1878; 3rd class in mod. hist. finals, June, 1880; B.A., July, 1880; M.A., 1911; classical prof. at the Roy. Coll., Mauritius, June, 1881; précis writer, col. sec.'s office, Feb., and 2nd asst. col. sec., Apr., 1889; ag. col. sec., Br. Hon.
author of "Thoughts on Modern Church Work."

RS, CECIL GEORGE LEWIS.—B. 1903; ed., Dul's Sch.; and Oxford; classical schol., I Coll., 1921-25; 1st cls. classical mods., 1st cls., lit., hum., 1925; apptd. after t. exam., asst. prin., Dominions Office, 21st 1925; pvt. sec. to permit. under-sec., for affrs., 14th Nov., 1928; asst. pvt. sec. to S. for Dom. Affrs. (Mr. J. H. Thomas), June, 1930; ditto; to Mr. J. H. Thomas of S. for Dom. affrs. and for theCols., Aug., 1931; accompanied U.K. delegation np. Economic Cnfece., Ottawa, 1932; 1st Jan., 1933; accompanied U.K. air m to Canada and U.S.A., Nov.-Dec., KES, GEORGE ROGNVALD M.A. (Liv.). 889; cadet, S. Stltltns., Nov., 1913; ag. 3rd Penang, July, 1914; attd., censor's office, passed cadet, 1917; ag. asst. prot. hinese, Spore, Apr., 1917; asst. regir. and expts. (war trade dept.) Spore, 1917; ag. asst. prot. of Chinese (in addition) 1918; ceased to perform duties in war trade ag. asst. prot. of Chinese, Spore, Sept., ag. 3rd mag., Spore, in addn., Dec., ag. 2nd asst. prot. of Chinese, Spore, 1920; supernm. offr., cls. IV., Nov., 1920; 1st supt., govt. monopolies and asst. prot. of Malacca, June, 1921; asst. prot., Chinese, e., Sept., 1924; ols. III., Nov., 1925; prot., Kedah, Dec., 1926; ag. prot., Chinese, Igor and Pahang, June, 1929 and Sept.; offr., cls. II., prot., Chinese, Perak, Nov.; ag. prot., Chinese, Selangor and Pahang, 1933; ag. immigrn. offr., S.S. and F.M.S., 1936.

ME, MARY KERR GODFREY.—B. 1903; ed., Ism Schl.; cadet and asst. dist. comsnr., Coast, 1928.

MES, Lieut.-Col. Sir GEORGE STEWART, M.G.(1932), K.B.E.(1928), C.M.G., D.S.O.—82; ed. Malvern Coll. and Sandhurst; ent. y. 1900; serv. S. African War (Queen's med., spas); Aden, 1903-04 (desps., D.S.O.); attd., Sudan Army, 1905 and Sudan govt., 1907; Blue expdn., 1908 (med.); promoted major, 1915 brevet lt.-col., 1917; A.D.C. to Sirdar and gov. of the Sudan, 1906-07; asst. dir. of intellige., 1908-12; pte. sec. and sec., gov. gen.'s (Sudan), 1913-16; European War (3 times t. in desps., med., brevet lt.-col.); attd. of high comsnr., Egypt, 1917-19; attd. y. of int., Egypt, 1919-20; dist. gov., Palestine, 1920; ch. sec., 1925; admstd. gov., Palestine, July to Sept., 1925 and May to Sept.; accredited rep. to mandates comsnr., 1926 and 1927; res. and commdr.-in-ch., Aden, 1928; and commdr.-in-ch., Tanganyika Territory, gov.-gen., Sudan, 1933.

YMONETTE, W. J.—B. 1878; pub. schl., her, Apr., 1898; 4th divn. comsnr., June, 1898; ag. ch. clk., recvr. gen. in treas. dept., 1922; confirmed in appt., Feb., 1924.

YMONS, CLAUDE TREVINE.—B. 1879; B.A., F.R.G.S.; vice-principal, govt. training Cevlon, Aug., 1908; asst. govt. analyst, 1912; ag. govt. analyst, in addn., Dec., govt. analyst, June, 1919; ag. regir., med. in addn., May to Dec., 1922.

ADMAN, JOHN LAD BROOKE, B.A. (Oxon).—Norwich Schl. and St. Edmund Hall, Oxford (Edsmiths' Exhibn., 1929); col. aud. dept., Feb., 1931; asst. audr., Uganda, Apr., 1931; asst. audr., Mauritius, Feb., 1936.

TAIT, HUGH NIMMO.—B. 1888; ed. at Clifton and St. John's Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. Math. Tripos, Part I. and II.; 1st cls. Nat. Science Tripos, Part I.; apptd. after compet. exam., clk., chief sec.'s office, Ireland, Oct., 1911; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Mar., 1912; ag. 1st class clk., 20th July, 1917; on mil. service from 27th Sept. to 9th Dec., 1918; sec. to Rhodesian Comsn., 1919-20; prin., 1st Apr., 1920; ag. asst. sec., D.O., 4th Sept., 1929; asst. sec., 24th Jan., 1930.

TAITT, HORACE VIBART.—B. 1887; ed. at Harrison Coll., Barbados; Island scholar, 1906; 3rd cls. class B.A., 1909; M.A., 1917; educn. offr., educn. dept., B. Guiana, 1914; ag. 2nd asst. inspr. of schools in 1914, 1915 and 1916; ag. 3rd cls. clk., educn. off., Jan.-Apr., 1917; ag. class. mast., Queen's Coll., Apr.-July, 1917; ag. asst. mast., do., Mar., 1930; asst. mast., 1934.

TATHAM, BERNARD MEABURN.—B. 1891; ed., Rossall Schl.; asst. accont., P.W.D., Uganda, May, 1921; ob. accont., Apr., 1922; asst. treas., Uganda, June, 1926, (with seniority from May, 1921); senr. asst. treas., Sept., 1934; senr. asst. treas., Gold Coast, Aug., 1936; ag. dep. treas., Sept., 1936.

TAYLOR, ARTHUR PERCY, M.C., 1914 (Mons Star).—B. 1892; ed. Colchester Royal Grammar Schl.; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1926; served with R.N.V.R., R.N.D., R.N.A.S. and R.A.F., 1914-19; severely wounded, 1917; asst. accont., P.W.D., Gold Coast, Jan., 1920; asst. commdt., Northern Territories constab., Sept., 1920; transf'd, to Gold Coast pol. asst. comsnr., pol., Nov., 1923; comsnr., pol. and in charge, C.I.D., 1926; seconded to Ashanti judiciary as ag. pol. mag., May, 1927; pol. mag., sup. ct. Gold Coast, June, 1928; crown coun., Sept., 1932; ag. solr.-gen. in 1933.

TAYLOR, EDWIN, C.M.G. (1936).—B. 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ.ser., and assigned to C.O. Jan. 1901; served with I.Y. in S. African war, 1901-02 (medal and four clasps); re-apptd. to 2nd div., and assigned to B. of T., 1902; clk., P.W.D., B.C. Africa Prov., July, 1906; treas. asst., Uganda, Jan., 1909; asst. treas., civil admin., German East Africa (occupied territory), Jan., 1917; treas., Seychelles, May, 1919; dep. treas., Uganda, Apr., 1923; ag. treas., May 1923 to 1924; senr. asst. treas., Sierra Leone, Apr., 1925; ag. treas., in 1925, 1926, 1928 and 1929; title altered to dep. treas., Jan., 1930; mem.
